NONE: › to have very good and detailed knowledge of something
熟諳；對…瞭如指掌

example: She knows her part in the play back to front.
她熟諳自己在劇中的角色。

NONE: › to know the difference between two things and therefore be able to recognize either, used especially to mean that you have a good knowledge and understanding of a particular subject
辨別；識別

example: Computer expert? He doesn't know a mouse from a modem! (= He knows nothing about computers.)
電腦專家？他連滑鼠和數據機都分不清！

NONE: C1 to know everything about a subject
對…瞭如指掌

example: He knows the system inside out.
他對該體系瞭如指掌。

NONE: › to have very good and detailed knowledge of something
精通；對…瞭如指掌

example: I know this area like the back of my hand.
我對這一地區瞭如指掌。

NONE: › to know all the important facts in a situation, especially the unpleasant ones
了解情況；（尤指）了解問題的癥結

example: You know the score - no payment till after the article is published.
你了解情況——文章發表後才付稿酬。

NONE: › to be familiar with how it feels to be or do something
了解…的感覺（或滋味）

example: She knows what it's like to go bankrupt - it happened to her 20 years ago.
她知道破產是甚麼滋味 — 20年前她就曾破產過。

NONE: › to have the skills and knowledge to do something effectively
掌握有效做某事的技能（或知識）

example: You don't need to tell me - I know what I'm doing!
你不用告訴我——我應付得了！

NONE: C1 to understand a subject because of your experience
作經驗之談

example: He doesn't know what he's talking about - he's never even been to Africa.
他在信口開河——他從沒去過非洲。

NONE: › If you know what's what, you have a lot of experience and can judge people and situations well.
在行；老練

example: Linda's been in the business for 30 years - she knows what's what.
蓮達從事這一行已經30年了——她很在行。

NONE: › If you do not know when you are well off, you do not understand that your present situation is good compared with other people's or with what it might be like.
知足

example: She's always complaining about her car - she doesn't know when she's well off (= she's lucky to have a car even if it's bad)!
她總是在抱怨自己的車不好——她根本就不知足。

NONE: C2 to know what your opinion or situation is
知道自己的立場；清楚自己的情況

example: I know where I stand on this issue - I'm against the war.
我很清楚自己在這個問題上的立場——我反對戰爭。
When we've paid all our debts we'll know where we stand.
等我們償清債務後，就清楚自己的情況如何了。

NONE: › to know who to be nice to and what to do in order to get an advantage for yourself
明白自已的利益所在，善為個人利益謀算
› to be certain about what you believe or want
有自己明確的想法（或願望）；有主見
› to accept your position within society, an organization, your family, etc. and to not want to improve it
安分守己；安於現狀

example: I just get on with my job and do as I'm told - I know my place.
我只是按吩咐做好我的工作——我很守本分。

NONE: C2 to have good practical skills and knowledge in a particular activity or subject
精通業務，在行
› to be familiar with a place or organization and able to act effectively within it
在行；熟悉
› a person who thinks that they know much more than other people
自以為無所不知的人
› practical knowledge and ability
實際知識；技術；技能

example: technical know-how
專業技能

NONE: › a person who thinks that they know much more than other people
自以為無所不知的人
› If you say to someone you know or see where they are coming from, you mean you understand why that person has a particular opinion, often although you do not have that opinion.
明白／知道（某人）為甚麼會那樣想

example: I would've taken the dog to the vet, but I could see where they were coming from.
是我的話，我會把狗送去看獸醫，但是我也明白他們為什麼會那麼想。

NONE: › able to be known
可知的；可認識的
› showing that you know about something, even when it has not been talked about
會意的，心照不宣的

example: a knowing look/glance/smile
會意的一望／一瞥／微笑

NONE: C2 in a way that shows you know about something
會意地；知情地
C2 If you do something knowingly, you do it knowing what will be its likely effect.
故意地，蓄意地

example: She smiled knowingly at him.
她會意地向他笑了笑。
I've never knowingly offended him.
我從未蓄意冒犯過他。

S or U: B1 [ S or U ] understanding of or information about a subject that you get by experience or study, either known by one person or by people generally
知識；學問；學識；了解；理解

U: › [ U ] the state of knowing about or being familiar with something

example: Her knowledge of English grammar is very extensive.
她的英語文法知識很廣博。
He has a limited knowledge of French.
他對法語所知有限。
The details of the scandal are now common knowledge (= familiar to most people).
醜聞的詳情現在眾所周知。
She started to photograph the documents, safe in the knowledge that (= knowing that) she wouldn't be disturbed for at least an hour.
她開始對文件拍照，確信至少一小時內不會有人打擾。
In this town there are only a couple of restaurants that to my knowledge (= judging from my personal experience and information) serve good food.
據我所知，這個鎮上只有幾家餐館菜餚不錯。
They both deny all knowledge of the affair.
他們倆完全否認知道此事。
It has come/been brought to our knowledge (= we have discovered) that several computers have gone missing.
我們發現有幾台電腦不見了。

NONE: C1 knowing a lot
知識淵博的；有見識的

example: He's very knowledgeable about German literature.
他精通德國文學。

NONE: B2 used to refer to something or someone that is familiar to or understood by people
知道的；聞名的；已知的
B1 If someone or something is known as a particular name, that person or thing is called by that name.
被稱作…的；以…聞名的
› to tell people about something so that it becomes publicly known
公佈，發表

example: These people are known criminals.
這些人是臭名遠播的罪犯。
There is no known reason for the accident.
事故的原因還不得而知。
He is known to the police because of his previous criminal record.
他因為有前科而在警方那裡「揚名」。
See also
well known
Local residents have made known their objections to the proposals.
當地居民發表聲明反對那些提議。
I made it known that I was not happy with the decision.
我公開聲明不滿這個決定。
